comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** in the tested scope, Back (Left, or Backspace with an empty filter) now returns the cursor to the parent row used to open the submenu. The restore works for keyboard and mouse entry and at each level of a nested history. It also follows the row by id when other parent rows are hidden while the submenu is open. If the saved row became disabled, the cursor moves to the next selectable row. One edge case remains for submenus opened from search results.

| Flow (default menu, harness run of the production functions) | Base: cursor after Back | Head: cursor after Back |
|---|---|---|
| Root, cursor to Style, Enter, Back | Apps | Style |
| Root › Setup › Defaults › Browser, Back three times | first row each time | Browser, Defaults, Setup |
| Enter Install while guarded rows above it are hidden, Back | Apps | Install |
| Click Update with the keyboard cursor on Apps, Back | Apps | Update |

### Back after opening a deeper search result lands on an unrelated row

With a filter active, the list includes matching submenus from deeper levels. When one of those is opened, `setActiveMenu` saves the filtered-list index and the deeper row's id. Back clears the filter and rebuilds the parent with only its own rows, so the id lookup finds no match. The filtered index is then applied to the unfiltered list.

```text
root, filter "browser"          saved on Enter
  0  Setup › Defaults › Browser
  1  Install › Browser   <-- Enter   { index: 1, itemId: "install.browser" }
  2  Remove › Browser

Back: filter cleared, root rebuilt unfiltered
  0  Apps
  1  Learn               <-- cursor (id not found, index 1 reused)
  ...
  5  Install             (row the submenu belongs under)
```

Observed with the default menu and no installed-app search results (installed apps can add results and shift the exact row). The base branch puts the cursor on the first row in the same flow. Search results that are direct children of the current menu, such as `style` from the top level, restore correctly.

**Impact:** cursor position only, with no wrong action. The search, open, Back flow ends on a row unrelated to the one chosen, which is less predictable than the previous first-row behavior.

**Suggested change:** when the picked row is not a direct child of the menu being left, save its ancestor that is (so Back lands on Install), or skip the index fallback when a filter was active. These approaches were not tested.

**Optional test improvement:** the reorder assertion in `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` moves `style` to index 0, which is also where the base code always puts the cursor, so that assertion alone passes against base. Moving the tracked row to a nonzero index other than the saved one (for example `[apps, style, learn]`, expecting 1) makes it fail on base and pass on head.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `7a7fb10` against base `quattro` (`d3cfd53`). The repository menu test passed on head and base in an isolated sandbox, using Deno's Node compatibility in place of Node. A harness ran the production navigation functions from both revisions against the default menu, with rendering, providers and the pointer gate stubbed. No running Omarchy Shell or graphical session was used, so row highlighting and scroll-into-view were assessed from source only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
